paper_takeaway: Quality-aware sparse fusion mainly improves regression error and noisy/incomplete-modality robustness, not necessarily average Macro-F1.
Uncertainty/credibility aggregation is best framed as calibration and high-range reliability control.
Anchor-guided decision refinement provides the cleanest classification contribution in this suite.
Tail-safety calibration is a safety trade-off: removing it can improve aggregate MAE while worsening high-range signed bias.
Personalization/conformal components should be evaluated by subject gain and reliability/robustness rather than average MAE alone.
